mainTopic: A נזיר's hair: full shaving, רובו ככולו, washing and combing, and repeated sins
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier proof: ציצית written next to כלאים teaches that a positive מצוה can override a prohibition. Then the גמרא returns to the rule that a נזיר, מצורע or לוי who shaves without a razor, or leaves two hairs, has done nothing. From this רב אחא בריה דרב איקא learns that רובו ככולו is Torah law, since the Torah had to spell out a full shave for a נזיר. The scholars of ארץ ישראל defend this proof against רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's objection. אביי and רבא then ask about leftover hairs that are shaved later or fall out, and רבינא rules that shaving a single last hair is no מצוה of shaving. A new משנה lets a נזיר wash and separate his hair but not comb it, and רבה explains that the whole משנה follows רבי שמעון because combing is done on purpose to remove loose hairs. רבי ישמעאל forbids washing with earth, and the גמרא's question about his exact wording ends in תיקו. The amud closes with a משנה teaching that a נזיר who keeps sinning is punished once, unless he was warned each time.

steps.title: Fringes may be made from wool and linen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier proof. The verse about ציצית, right next to the ban on כלאים, teaches that ציצית may be made from wool and linen together.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches that 'You shall make for yourself fringes' can be from them (wool and linen together).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a proof it started before this section. The verse about ציצית comes right next to the ban on mixing wool and linen, so ציצית may be made from that mix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two verses sit side by side, the Torah is teaching that the מצוה of ציצית overrides the prohibition of כלאים. From here we learn the general rule that a positive מצוה‎ (עשה) pushes aside a prohibition (לא תעשה).

keyTerms.meaning: From them, meaning from wool and linen together
The forbidden mix of wool and linen in clothing
A positive מצוה overrides a prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: ציצית placed next to כלאים teaches that a positive מצוה can override a prohibition.

phrases.english: This teaches that 'You shall make for yourself fringes' can be from them.
phrases.notes: דברים 22:12. 'From them' means from the wool and linen mentioned in the verse just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the derivation from the previous section that עשה דוחה לא תעשה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Wool ציצית may go on a linen garment, which shows a positive מצוה overrides a prohibition.

steps.title: Shaving without a razor or leaving two hairs does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes an earlier teaching: if a נזיר, מצורע or לוי shaves without a razor, or leaves two hairs, the shaving is worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: All of them who shaved without a razor, or who left two hairs, have done nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a teaching it quoted earlier about the people who must shave: נזיר, מצורע and לויים. It quotes it again to set up the next statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things ruin the shave: using a tool other than a razor, or leaving even two hairs. So for these people the shave must be complete. That is the detail the next step builds on.

keyTerms.meaning: They have done nothing at all; it does not count

phrases.english: The Master said:
And all of them who shaved not with a razor,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the נזיר, the מצורע and the לויים, who all have to shave.

phrases.english: or who left two hairs —
have done nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by re-quoting the teaching about who must shave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a נזיר, מצורע or לוי, a shave without a razor or with two hairs left over is invalid.

steps.title: רב אחא: 'most counts like all' is Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא learns from the two-hairs rule that, in general, רובו ככולו is a Torah principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: This shows that 'most of something is like all of it' is Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא draws a general rule from the teaching we just read. He says it shows that רובו ככולו applies on a Torah level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It sounds backwards: the teaching needed the whole head shaved, so how does it show that 'most' is enough? The idea, explained in the next steps, is that the Torah had to make a special point here, so in other places 'most' counts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is to say': a rule drawn from a source
Most of something counts like all of it
By Torah law, not just a rabbinic rule

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב אחא is saying 'most' is enough for a נזיר. For a נזיר the whole head is needed. He is saying that because the נזיר is a special case, everywhere else 'most' is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: רובו ככולו is a principle used all over הלכה, so its level (Torah or rabbinic) matters a great deal.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, said:
That is to say,
the majority of something is like all of it by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from the rule just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רובו ככולו is a Torah-level principle.

steps.title: How do we know this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the two-hairs rule proves רובו ככולו.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב אחא learned his rule from the shaving teaching. This short question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is real because the teaching seems to point the other way: it demands the full head. The גמרא wants to see the reasoning that turns a 'whole head' rule into a 'most is enough' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From what? How do we know?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב אחא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the two-hairs rule for a נזיר shows that רובו ככולו is Torah law.

steps.title: The Torah spelled out a full shave only for a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The Torah specially wrote 'On the seventh day he shall shave it' for a נזיר. So only here is the whole head needed; elsewhere 'most' is like all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah spelled out for a נזיר, 'On the seventh day he shall shave it,' only here is all of it needed. In general, most of something counts like all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the proof. The Torah made a special statement about a נזיר's shave, which shows that only there is the whole head needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'most' never counted, the Torah would not need to make a special point that a נזיר shaves everything. Because it did, we learn that the full-head rule is the exception. The normal rule is רובו ככולו.

keyTerms.meaning: Since the Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') revealed or spelled out

steps.whatToRemember: A special Torah rule requiring 'all' in one case shows that in ordinary cases 'most' is enough.

phrases.english: From the fact that the Merciful One revealed regarding a nazirite
'On the seventh day he shall shave it' —
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:9. The same verse already said he shaves his head, so the גמרא reads this extra mention as demanding the whole head.

phrases.english: it is here that it does not count until there is all of it.
But in general, the majority is like all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah's special phrasing for a נזיר shows that requiring the whole is an exception, so in general רובו ככולו.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: that verse is about an impure נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא objects. The verse is about a נזיר טמא, but our teaching covers every נזיר, even a pure one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא objected: This verse is written about an impure נזיר!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא attacks the proof. He points out that the verse used is about a נזיר who became impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about two hairs applies to every נזיר, including a pure one (נזיר טהור) finishing his term. The verse only speaks of a נזיר טמא, so it can't be the source for the full-head rule for everyone. That weakens the proof for רובו ככולו.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר who became ritually impure

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, objected to this:
This is written about an impure nazirite!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'ביום השביעי יגלחנו' as the source for the full-head rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse speaks only of a נזיר טמא, while the teaching covers a נזיר טהור too, so the verse can't be the source for the general rule.

steps.title: The West laughs: pure and impure נזיר learn from each other
steps.stepSummary: The scholars in ארץ ישראל laughed at the objection. An impure נזיר learns the razor rule from a pure one, so a pure נזיר can learn the two-hairs rule from an impure one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at this in the West: How do we know an impure נזיר shaves with a razor? We learn it from a pure נזיר. So let the pure נזיר learn from the impure one: just as an impure נזיר who leaves two hairs has done nothing, so too a pure נזיר who leaves two hairs has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of ארץ ישראל reject רבי יוסי's objection. They show that the rules of the pure and impure נזיר are shared both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The razor rule is written for a pure נזיר, and an impure נזיר learns it from there. If that comparison works one way, it works the other way too. So the full-head rule written for the impure נזיר also applies to the pure one, and the proof for רובו ככולו stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
After all; let's think it through
A ritually pure נזיר finishing his term

steps.whatToRemember: The pure and impure נזיר learn from each other, so the full-head rule covers both, and the proof that רובו ככולו is Torah law stands.

phrases.english: They laughed at this in the West:
After all, from where do we know that an impure nazirite shaves with a razor?
He learns it from a pure nazirite.
So let a pure nazirite come
and learn from an impure nazirite:

phrases.aramaic: מָה טָמֵא כִּי שַׁיַּיר שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת —
phrases.english: Just as an impure one, when he leaves two hairs,
has done nothing,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, כִּי שַׁיַּיר שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת —
phrases.english: so too here, when he leaves two hairs,
he has done nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's objection from step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole objection that the verse is limited to a נזיר טמא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The objection ignores that the pure and impure נזיר already learn shaving rules from each other, so the comparison works in both directions.

steps.title: אביי asks about shaving the two leftover hairs after the head grew back
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks about a נזיר who left two hairs, let his hair grow back, and then shaved just those two hairs. Does his shaving now count?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: A נזיר shaved but left two hairs. His hair grew back, and then he went back and shaved those two hairs. What is the law? Do those hairs still hold back his shaving, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a new question that builds on the rule that two leftover hairs hold back a נזיר's shaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know two leftover hairs spoil the shaving. Now the hairs are finally cut, but only after the rest of the head has grown back. Does this late shaving finish the job, or does cutting two hairs on a full head mean nothing, so he must shave everything again? The גמרא gives no answer here.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question the גמרא tries to settle)
They hold back (they stop the shaving from counting)

phrases.english: Abaye asked:
A nazir who shaved and left over two hairs,
his head grew back, and he went back and shaved them,
what is the law?
Do they hold it back, or not?
phrases.notes: "They" means the two leftover hairs. Do they still stop his shaving from counting, even though he shaved them later?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that uses the two-hairs rule discussed above
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does shaving the two leftover hairs later, after the head grew back, complete the נזיר's shaving?

steps.title: רבא asks about one hair shaved and one hair falling out
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about a נזיר who left two hairs, then shaved one, and the other fell out by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: A נזיר shaved and left two hairs. Then he shaved one of them, and the other one fell out. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks another question about the two leftover hairs. This time one is shaved and the other falls out on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the head now counts as fully shaved, since one of the last two hairs was never cut with a razor. The next step will challenge whether this is really what רבא meant to ask.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
A nazir who shaved and left two hairs,
and he shaved one, and one fell out. What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question on the same topic of two leftover hairs
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If one leftover hair is shaved and the other falls out, is the shaving complete?

steps.title: רב אחא challenges the wording of רבא's question
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי says to רבינא that רבא could not be asking this, because it is just like shaving one hair at a time, which is clearly allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדיפתי said to רבינא: Is רבא really asking whether one may shave hair by hair?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדיפתי attacks רבא's question as it was told. He says the case is too obvious to be a real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shaving the whole head one hair at a time is surely a valid shaving. In רבא's case as told, he was still shaving when he cut one of the two hairs, so it looks just like shaving hair by hair. So רבא could not have been unsure about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Hair by hair, one at a time
Is he asking? Is it a question for him?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
Shaving hair by hair,
is that something Rava is asking about?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רבא's question was told
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רבא's question was worded (shaved one, then one fell out)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is the same as shaving hair by hair, which is clearly valid, so it is not a real question

steps.title: Reversing the order: one hair fell out, then he shaved the other
steps.stepSummary: The question is fixed: first one hair fell out, and only then did he shave the last hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: one hair fell out, and then he shaved the other one. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רבא's question by reversing the order of what happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the hair falls out first, so when he picks up the razor only one hair is left. The real question is whether shaving one single hair counts as finishing the shaving.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (fix the wording to this)

phrases.english: Rather, say:
One fell out and he shaved one. What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by restating רבא's question
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the case (reversing the order of events)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא asked about shaving one hair and then the other falling out
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא asked about one hair falling out first and then shaving the single last hair

steps.title: רבינא rules: no shaving here, no hair here
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that in this case there is no valid shaving, and no hair either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: There is no shaving here, and there is no hair here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the fixed question. He rules that this does not count as a proper shaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once one hair fell out, only a single hair was left, and shaving one hair is not a real act of shaving. His short wording sounds odd, so the next step questions it.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבינא answering רב אחא.

phrases.aramaic: גִּילּוּחַ אֵין כָּאן, שֵׂעָר אֵין כָּאן.
phrases.english: There is no shaving here; there is no hair here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reworded question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Shaving the single last hair after the other fell out is not a valid shaving

steps.title: If there is no hair, then the head is shaved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבינא's wording: if no hair is left, then the head is shaved!
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is no hair here, then there is shaving here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבינא's words because they seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the head has no hair left, it looks fully shaved. So how can רבינא say there is no shaving? The גמרא needs to explain what he meant.

phrases.english: If there is no hair here,
then there is shaving here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רבינא's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's phrase 'no shaving here, no hair here'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A head with no hair is a shaved head, so the two halves of his statement seem to clash

steps.title: The head is bare, but the מצוה of shaving was not done
steps.stepSummary: רבינא meant: even though no hair is left, the מצוה of shaving was not done.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: Even though there is no hair here, the מצוה of shaving is not here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבינא's words. A bare head is not enough. The מצוה of shaving also has to be done properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head ends up bare, but the נזיר did not finish shaving the first time. The second time he shaved only one hair, which is less than a real shaving. So the result is a bare head with no מצוה of shaving.
steps.whatToRemember: For a נזיר, a bare head alone is not enough. The מצוה is the act of shaving, and shaving a single last hair after the other fell out does not count.

phrases.english: This is what he meant:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשֵּׂעָר אֵין כָּאן,
phrases.english: Even though there is no hair here,
the מצוה of shaving is not here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge on רבינא's wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining what the words really mean
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No shaving' seemed to mean the head was not bare
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No shaving' means the מצוה of shaving was not done, even though the head is bare

steps.title: משנה: a נזיר may wash and separate his hair but not comb it
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a נזיר may wash his hair and separate it with his hands, but he may not comb it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A נזיר may wash his hair and separate it with his hands, but he may not comb it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: what a נזיר may do to care for his hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing and separating the hair by hand are allowed. Combing is not allowed. The משנה gives the rule without a reason, and the גמרא will discuss it next.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A nazir may wash and separate his hair,
but he may not comb it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר may wash and separate his hair by hand, but may not comb it

steps.title: Who is the author of the washing rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that a נזיר may wash and separate his hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: He may wash and separate his hair. Who is the author of this rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking whose opinion it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing and separating hair can make hairs fall out, and a נזיר may not remove hair. So the גמרא wants to know which תנא would allow this when hair might fall.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Separates the hairs with the hands
Who is it? (Who is the author?)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
He may wash and separate his hair: who is the author?
phrases.notes: These words are quoted from the משנה we just saw in step 15.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה from step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא allows a נזיר to wash and separate his hair even though hairs might fall out.

steps.title: First half follows רבי שמעון, second half seems to follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Washing is allowed according to רבי שמעון, who permits an unintended act. But the ban on combing seems to follow the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי שמעון, who says an act done without intending the forbidden result is allowed. But the words 'he may not comb' bring us to the opinion of the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the washing rule follows רבי שמעון. But it then notices that the combing ban seems to follow the רבנן instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that if you don't intend the forbidden result (hair falling out), the act is allowed. So washing is fine. But combing is forbidden, even though the נזיר also doesn't mean to pull hair, so that part looks like the רבנן, who forbid even an unintended act.

keyTerms.meaning: An act where the forbidden result is not intended
We have come to (the opinion of)
The Sages, who argue with רבי שמעון

steps.confusionAlert: Washing and combing both might pull out hair without the נזיר meaning to. That is why it looks strange that one is allowed and the other forbidden.

phrases.english: It is רבי שמעון,
who says: an act that is not intended is permitted.
But 'he may not comb':
we have come to the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דְּאָמַר: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who wrote the משנה, but splits it between two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The washing part follows רבי שמעון; the combing ban seems to follow the רבנן.

steps.title: Can one משנה follow two different opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: is the first half by רבי שמעון and the second half by the רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the first part רבי שמעון and the last part the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the answer it just gave. It is hard to say one short משנה switches authors in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we expect a single משנה to follow one consistent opinion. Splitting it between רבי שמעון and the רבנן is a forced reading, so the גמרא looks for a better explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה

phrases.english: The first part is רבי שמעון
and the last part is the רבנן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the split-author answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי שמעון in its first half and the רבנן in its second half.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single משנה should not be split between two opposing opinions without a good reason.

steps.title: רבה: the whole משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that combing is different: anyone who combs really means to remove loose hairs, so it is an intended act.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The whole משנה is רבי שמעון. Anyone who combs intends to remove loose, dangling hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה fixes the problem by showing that the combing ban also fits רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון only allows acts where the forbidden result is not intended. Combing is not like that: a person combs exactly in order to pull out loose hairs. So combing counts as intentional hair removal and is forbidden even for רבי שמעון, while washing stays allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה follows רבי שמעון: washing is allowed because hair falling is not intended, but combing is forbidden because a person combs in order to remove loose hairs.

phrases.english: רבה said:
The whole of it is רבי שמעון,
anyone who combs:
intends to remove dangling hairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: combing is actually an intended act.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Combing, like washing, was thought to be an unintended act, so its ban seemed to follow the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Combing is done in order to remove loose hairs, so even רבי שמעון forbids it; the whole משנה follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: no washing hair with earth
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: רבי ישמעאל says a נזיר may not wash his hair with earth, because it makes hair fall out.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי ישמעאל says: He may not wash his hair with earth, because it makes the hair fall out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next משנה, with a new rule from רבי ישמעאל about washing with earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing with water is allowed, but earth was used as a cleaning agent and it pulls out hair. Since a נזיר may not remove hair, רבי ישמעאל forbids it.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
רבי ישמעאל says:
He may not wash his hair with earth,
because it makes the hair fall out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: לֹא יָחוֹף בַּאֲדָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next rule in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר may not wash his hair with earth, because earth makes hair fall out.

steps.title: What is the exact wording of רבי ישמעאל's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה says 'because it removes hair' or 'because of the kind that removes hair'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They asked: Did we learn 'because it makes the hair fall out', or perhaps we learned 'because of the one that makes hair fall out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the exact words of רבי ישמעאל's reason. There are two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading one: all earth removes hair, so that is why it is forbidden. Reading two: only some earth removes hair, but all earth is forbidden because of the kind that does.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the Sages)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A question was asked before them:
Did we learn 'because it makes the hair fall out',
phrases.notes: In this reading, 'it' means earth in general: all earth removes hair.

phrases.english: or perhaps we learned 'because of the one that makes hair fall out'?
phrases.notes: Here the idea is that some earth removes hair and some doesn't, and all is forbidden because of the kind that does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the exact wording of the משנה in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's reason says all earth removes hair, or that all earth is forbidden because some kinds remove hair.

steps.title: What difference does the wording make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two readings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the exact wording matters in practice. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before deciding between the two readings, the גמרא wants to know if they lead to different rulings. If no ruling changes, the question would not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 21 by asking what difference the two readings make.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical ruling that would differ between the two readings of the משנה.

steps.title: The practical difference: earth that does not remove hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two readings differ when the earth is a kind that does not make hair fall out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is a case where there is earth that does not remove hair. If the משנה says 'because it removes hair', then earth that we know does not remove hair is fine. But if it says 'because of the kind that removes hair', then a נזיר may not wash with any earth at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from step 22. It shows exactly when the two readings of the משנה would give different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the reading 'because it removes hair', the ban depends on what each kind of earth actually does, so harmless earth is allowed. With the reading 'because of the kind that removes', the ban covers all earth because of the kind that does remove hair. Then even harmless earth is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Earth or soil, used here like a shampoo for washing the hair
Fine, it is good, it is allowed
Not at all, in no case

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings agree that earth which removes hair is forbidden. They argue only about earth that does not remove hair.

phrases.english: For example, where there is earth that does not remove hair.
If you say we learned in the משנה, 'because it removes hair',
then where we know that it does not remove hair, it is fine.
But if you say the משנה reads 'because of the kind that removes hair',
then he may not use any earth at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 about the practical difference between the two readings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The readings differ about earth that does not remove hair. Under 'because it removes' such earth is allowed. Under 'because of the kind that removes' all earth is forbidden.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot decide which reading is correct, so the question stands (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without an answer. We do not know which wording the משנה really has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source was found that settles the question from step 21. So it is left open whether a נזיר may wash with earth that does not remove hair.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a נזיר may wash his hair with harmless earth stays a תיקו, because we do not know if the משנה said 'because it removes' or 'because of the kind that removes'.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 21 without a decision, even after the difference was explained in step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The wording of רבי ישמעאל's משנה stays in doubt, and so does the ruling about earth that does not remove hair.

steps.title: New משנה: one set of lashes or many for a נזיר who keeps sinning
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר who drinks, shaves, or becomes impure from the dead many times in one day is punished once, unless he was warned each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נזיר who was drinking wine all day is punished only once. If people told him 'Don't drink! Don't drink!' and he kept drinking, he is punished for each time. If he kept shaving all day, he is punished only once. If they told him 'Don't shave! Don't shave!' and he kept shaving, he is punished for each time. If he kept becoming impure from the dead all day, he is punished only once. If they told him 'Don't become impure! Don't become impure!' and he kept doing it, he is punished for each time.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how many sets of lashes a נזיר gets when he breaks his נזירות over and over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing the same forbidden act many times in a row counts as one sin. A new warning before each act turns each act into a separate punishable sin. The משנה gives the same rule for all three things a נזיר must avoid: wine, shaving, and impurity from the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: He is liable only once (one set of lashes)
Becoming ritually impure from a dead body

steps.confusionAlert: What counts is the number of warnings he was given, not simply how many times he drank or shaved.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן כׇּל הַיּוֹם —
phrases.english: MISHNA: A נזיר who was drinking wine all day
is liable only once.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: ״אַל תִּשְׁתֶּה״ ״אַל תִּשְׁתֶּה״, וְהוּא שׁוֹתֶה —
phrases.english: If they said to him, 'Don't drink, don't drink,' and he drinks,
he is liable for each and every one.
If he was shaving all day,
he is liable only once.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: ״אַל תְּגַלֵּחַ״ ״אַל תְּגַלֵּחַ״, וְהוּא מְגַלֵּחַ —
phrases.english: If they said to him, 'Don't shave, don't shave,' and he shaves,
he is liable for each and every one.
If he was becoming impure from the dead all day,
he is liable only once.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: ״אַל תִּטַּמֵּא״ ״אַל תִּטַּמֵּא״, וְהוּא מִטַּמֵּא —
phrases.english: If they said to him, 'Don't become impure, don't become impure,' and he becomes impure,
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן כׇּל הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the hair-washing question was left as תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeating a נזיר's forbidden act counts as one sin, but each separate warning makes each act a separate punishable sin.
